findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral connector like "Separately," or remove the transition word entirely.
findings.location: Program Overview, second paragraph ("Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter.")
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this sentence parallels the prior one (publishing a log to a shared folder), but tracking a budget internally is not a similar action; the connector is logically mismatched.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" vs. "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Merge these into a single section with one authoritative owner and cadence for the reimbursement log.
findings.location: Program Overview (first paragraph) vs. the later "Overview" section near the end of the document
findings.violation: The document states two different owners (people operations office vs. benefits team) and two different cadences (each quarter vs. after open enrollment) for publishing the same reimbursement log.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. ... Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a single conjunctive statement, e.g., "The stipend is available only when the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each conditional sentence is phrased as if that condition alone triggers eligibility ("can apply"), but the closing sentence requires all three conditions jointly - the individual statements contradict the conjunctive rule.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this anecdote or replace it with a general policy rule, e.g., "If the primary approver is unavailable, the backup reviewer completes sign-off within the standard timeline."
findings.location: How to Apply section, final paragraph
findings.violation: This is a narrative account of a specific incident (an untrained backup reviewer), not a general policy statement, and it's out of place in a policy document; it also undermines the timeline promised later.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days" vs. "the review takes longer because the manager ... is traveling"
findings.fix: Reconcile the two statements - either state that the two-day SLA has documented exceptions for approver absence, or remove the conflicting anecdote.
findings.location: Approval Timeline section, first paragraph, compared to How to Apply's final paragraph
findings.violation: The document promises a fixed two-business-day review window in one section while another section describes an open-ended delay due to an untrained backup reviewer, directly contradicting the stated SLA.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Rewrite in plain language, e.g., "The manager may use discretion when applying the standard review checklist."
findings.violation: The legalistic phrasing ("pursuant to," "notwithstanding") is stylistically inconsistent with the plain language used throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist" vs. "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the approved-equipment list is a hard requirement or subject to manager discretion, and state it consistently in one place.
findings.location: Required Documentation section, first line, compared to Approval Timeline
findings.violation: One section implies the manager can override the checklist at will, while the other states approval is contingent on strictly matching the approved list - these are in tension.

findings.evidence: "the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time"
findings.fix: Simplify to "This reimburses costs the employee already paid."
findings.violation: This phrasing is unnecessarily convoluted; it simply means the payment reimburses the employee, but is buried in filler wording ("at this point in time").

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first line
findings.violation: The document switches from third-person ("the employee," "the manager") to second-person ("you," "we"), an inconsistent voice compared to every other section.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second line
findings.violation: "Similarly" incorrectly frames the device-limit rule as parallel to the photo-check requirement; the two are unrelated rules.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Payment Processing") or replace it with actual term definitions, and vary the phrasing to avoid repetition.
findings.violation: The heading promises terminology definitions, but the content describes a process instead; it also repeats the phrase "the stipend item" three times in three sentences, which reads as stilted and mismatched to the section title.

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" vs. "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" (Reimbursement Amounts) vs. "the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle" (Program Coordination)
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single statement identifying one responsible party and one consistent timeline for disbursement.
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, compared to Reimbursement Amounts and Program Coordination sections
findings.violation: The document gives three different actors (Payroll, finance office, benefits team) and three different timelines (after monthly review, within one pay cycle, next pay cycle) for releasing the same reimbursement, without reconciling them.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate content or merge it into "How to Apply," using consistent third-person phrasing.
findings.violation: This duplicates content already covered in the "How to Apply" section and again shifts to second-person voice inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this section into "How to Apply" or clarify it as a distinct, ordered step list.
findings.violation: This section duplicates the process already described in "How to Apply" and is awkwardly phrased, leaving unclear whether receipt upload is part of the "beginning" step or a separate subsequent step.

findings.evidence: Heading "## Overview" duplicating "## Program Overview," with "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Delete this duplicate section or merge its content into "Program Overview," resolving the contradiction noted above.
findings.violation: Having two differently-worded sections with nearly identical headings ("Program Overview" and "Overview") that state conflicting facts about the same process is confusing and suggests unmerged duplicate content.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate sentence from one of the two locations.
findings.violation: This sentence is a verbatim duplicate of a sentence already present in the "Program Overview" section.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate this finance-review step into the "Approval Timeline" section so the full approval sequence and its effect on timing is clear.
findings.violation: This introduces an additional approval gate (finance review for requests over $200) that is never mentioned in "Approval Timeline," creating ambiguity about how this step fits into the stated two-business-day manager review and overall payout timeline.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what constitutes a "repeat" request (e.g., "a second request for the same equipment category by the same employee within the quarter").
findings.violation: The term "repeats" is undefined - it's unclear whether this means the same employee, same device category, same dollar amount, or something else, making the rule unenforceable as written.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Either add actual content about how employees can ask questions or receive policy updates, or rename the section to match its content (e.g., "Vendor List").
findings.location: Questions and Updates section (final section of document)
findings.violation: The heading promises guidance on questions and updates, but the content only describes a vendor list unrelated to anything mentioned elsewhere in the document, and no contact information or update process is actually provided.
